cond_0001.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Clarification from the agency: Your application will be considered if you are a: Current or former career/career-conditional; Reinstatement eligible; Special Appointing Authority (i.e., Military Spouse, Land and Base Management, VRA, 30% Veteran, Sch A) eligible; VEOA eligible Veteran; ICTAP eligible; or OPM Interchange Agreement eligible.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As a Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings.
Conducting routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative inspection and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.
cond_0001.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.
""Federal Regulations state no [Company name masked] employee, his/her spouse, or his/her minor child shall have, directly or indirectly, any financial interest, including compensated employment, stock, or proprietary interest in the alcohol, tobacco, firearms or explosives industries. You should be aware that you may be asked to relinquish any ownership of or interests in the alcohol, tobacco, firearms or explosives industries before a determination can be made whether access to [Company name masked] information, information technology systems, and/or facilities can be authorized.""

cond_0001.inclusion: [Company name masked] is an equal opportunity employer, committed to achieving diversity within the workforce and creating an inclusive working environment. The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, including:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State, and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0045.intro:
We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team at [Company name masked], a law enforcement agency within the [Location masked] Department of Justice. [Company name masked] works to protect communities from violent crime, illegal firearms and explosives use, arson, terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol and tobacco products. The agency coordinates with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to share information, provide training, conduct research, and apply technology in support of public safety.
This job is open to the public.
Your application will be considered if you are a: Current or former career/career-conditional; Reinstatement eligible; Special Appointing Authority (i.e., Military Spouse, Land and Base Management, VRA, 30% Veteran, Sch A) eligible; VEOA eligible Veteran; ICTAP eligible; or OPM Interchange Agreement eligible.
cond_0045.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to support the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will work as part of an all-source intelligence analysis team, sharing responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Coordinating analytical research on criminal or regulatory data and contributing to informational reports.
Working with colleagues to identify and select appropriate software for automating charts, graphs, and similar materials for use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Supporting ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities through routine intelligence-related tasks.
Assisting in the analysis of database information and helping produce output.

Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings.

Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.

Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-7 grade level in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree.
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0116.intro:
We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team at [Company name masked], a law enforcement agency within the [Location masked] Department of Justice. This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to own the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will operate as an all-source intelligence analyst, taking full accountability for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0116.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, you will:
Lead analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and deliver informational reports.
Determine and select appropriate software to produce charts, graphs, and other visual outputs for use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Execute routine intelligence-related tasks in direct support of ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Conduct analysis of database information and drive production of output.
cond_0116.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, including:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State, and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0130.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Your application will be considered if you are a: Current or former career/career-conditional; Reinstatement eligible; Special Appointing Authority (i.e., Military Spouse, Land and Base Management, VRA, 30% Veteran, Sch A) eligible; VEOA eligible Veteran; ICTAP eligible; or OPM Interchange Agreement eligible.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of intelligence analysis and how information from different sources fits together.
cond_0130.responsibilities:
As a Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings.
Conducting routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative inspection and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.
cond_0130.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-7 grade level in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree.
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0270.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to support the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will work as part of an all-source intelligence analysis team, sharing responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area.
cond_0270.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Coordinating analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and contributing to informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software to help automate various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Supporting ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities for the assigned office through routine intelligence-related tasks.
Assisting with analysis of database information and contributing to output.

Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National. Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation. Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Qualifications
To qualify for GS-9, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-7.
GS-9 - You qualify if you possess one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-7 grade level in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information; and
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases; and
Generating statistical/relational reports; and
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies.
OR
Master's or equivalent graduate degree OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
OR
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
OR
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience to qualify for this position. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.

You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.

Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As a Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings.

Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.
cond_0293.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Must meet the time-in-grade requirement by the closing date of this announcement
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.

You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects communities from violent criminals and criminal organizations, illegal use and trafficking of firearms, illegal use and storage of explosives, acts of arson and bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol and tobacco products. The agency coordinates with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, and technology.
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. The role functions as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0313.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Conducting routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Conducting analysis of database information and producing output.
cond_0313.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment as determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one-year probationary period.
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement.
New employees must sign a mobility agreement. Applicants who decline to sign will be removed from the hiring process.
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, performing the following:

Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases.
Generating statistical/relational reports.
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State, and Local government and law enforcement agencies.
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree; OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree.
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
A combination of graduate-level education and specialized experience. Only graduate-level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, a copy of unofficial or official transcripts must be provided.
All academic degrees and coursework must be completed at a college or university accredited or pre-accredited by a body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.

Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, including:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State, and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.

Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.

Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0386.intro:
We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team at [Company name masked], a law enforcement agency within the [Location masked] Department of Justice. This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to own the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will operate as an all-source intelligence analyst, taking full accountability for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0386.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, you will:
Lead analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and deliver informational reports.
Determine and select appropriate software to produce charts, graphs, and other visual outputs for use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Execute routine intelligence-related tasks in direct support of ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Conduct analysis of database information and drive production of output.
cond_0386.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Minimum Requirements
One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-7 in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector, including:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases
Generating statistical/relational reports
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State, and Local government and law enforcement agencies
Preferred Requirements
Master's or equivalent graduate degree, OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
LL.B. Or J.D., if related
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0441.intro:
We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team at [Company name masked], a law enforcement agency within the [Location masked] Department of Justice. [Company name masked] works to protect communities from violent crime, illegal firearms and explosives use, arson, terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol and tobacco products. The agency coordinates with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to share information, provide training, conduct research, and apply technology in support of public safety.
This job is open to the public.
Your application will be considered if you are a: Current or former career/career-conditional; Reinstatement eligible; Special Appointing Authority (i.e., Military Spouse, Land and Base Management, VRA, 30% Veteran, Sch A) eligible; VEOA eligible Veteran; ICTAP eligible; or OPM Interchange Agreement eligible.
cond_0441.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to support the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. You will work as part of an all-source intelligence analysis team, sharing responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area.
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Coordinating analytical research on criminal or regulatory data and contributing to informational reports.
Working with colleagues to identify and select appropriate software for automating charts, graphs, and similar materials for use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Supporting ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities through routine intelligence-related tasks.
Assisting in the analysis of database information and helping produce output.

cond_0445.intro:
[Company name masked] is a law enforcement agency in the [Location masked] Department of Justice that protects our communities from violent criminals/criminal organizations, illegal use/trafficking of firearms, illegal use/storage of explosives, acts of arson/bombings, acts of terrorism, and illegal diversion of alcohol/tobacco products. We partner with communities, industries, law enforcement, and public safety agencies to safeguard the public through information sharing, training, research, & technology.
This job is open to the public.
Your application will be considered if you are a: Current or former career/career-conditional; Reinstatement eligible; Special Appointing Authority (i.e., Military Spouse, Land and Base Management, VRA, 30% Veteran, Sch A) eligible; VEOA eligible Veteran; ICTAP eligible; or OPM Interchange Agreement eligible.
People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the kind of analytical and intelligence work involved.
cond_0445.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
As a Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, your typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports. Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings. Conducting routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative inspection and intelligence activities for the assigned office. Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.
cond_0445.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National. Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation. Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service. May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
To qualify for GS-9, candidates must also have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-7.
GS-9 - You qualify if you possess one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-7 grade level in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information; and Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases; and Generating statistical/relational reports; and Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies.
OR
Master's or equivalent graduate degree OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree
OR
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
OR
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience to qualify for this position. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
The Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.
Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP). The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy. To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and score 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility with your application to receive selection priority. Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.
Veterans Employment Opportunity Act (VEOA): VEOA allows eligible veterans to apply and compete for positions announced under merit promotion procedures when the hiring agency is recruiting from outside its own workforce. To be eligible for a Veteran Employment Opportunities Act (VEOA) appointment, a veteran must be honorably separated and either a preference eligible or have substantially completed three (3) or more years of continuous active military service. If you are applying for a Merit Promotion announcement and wish to be considered under the VEOA, you must submit a copy of the Member Copy 4 of your DD-214, in addition to any other required documents listed on this announcement.
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
Additional information
Additional vacancies may be filled from this vacancy announcement.
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended, that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, if you receive the link after the close of the announcement. To determine if you need RA, please review the Procedures for Requesting a Reasonable Accommodation for Online Assessments.

cond_0479.responsibilities:
This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analyses, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions, trends force in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect the national security. Performs as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for the project and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.

Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and generating informational reports. Identifying and selecting appropriate software for use in automating various charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials and hearings. Conducting routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative inspection and intelligence activities for the assigned office. Conducting some analysis of database information and produces output.

We are looking for an Intelligence Research Specialist to join our team. This position is located under the Office of Intelligence Operations, Criminal Intelligence Division, Analysis Production Branch in [Location masked].
The primary purpose of this position is to perform work in the collection, analysis, evaluation, interpretation, and dissemination of information on conditions and trends in foreign and domestic areas that directly or indirectly affect national security. The role functions as an all-source intelligence analyst with responsibility for projects and activities within a specifically defined geographical or functional area of responsibility.
cond_0502.responsibilities:
As an Intelligence Research Specialist, GS-0132-9, typical work assignments may include:
Conducting analytical research on criminal or regulatory related data and producing informational reports.
Identifying and selecting appropriate software for automating charts, graphs, etc. For use in cases, trials, and hearings.
Carrying out routine intelligence-related tasks in support of ongoing investigative, inspection, and intelligence activities for the assigned office.
Analyzing database information and producing output.
cond_0502.requirements:
Conditions of Employment
The time-in-grade requirement must be met by the closing date of this announcement. The qualification requirements listed below must be met by the closing date of the announcement.
This is a non-bargaining unit position.
MOBILITY PLAN: New employees hired pursuant to this vacancy announcement must sign a mobility agreement. The purpose of [Company name masked]'s mobility policy is to enhance career development and progression, and achieve mission and business effectiveness. To accomplish these objectives, the mobility plan will facilitate the movement of employees through special short-term assignments or permanent reassignments throughout the Bureau. Applicants who decline to sign a mobility agreement, as required, will be removed from the hiring process.
Key Requirements
Must be a [Location masked] Citizen or National.
Suitable for Federal employment determined by background investigation.
Must be registered or exempt from the Selective Service.
May be required to serve a one year probationary period.
Qualifications
To qualify for GS-9, candidates must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level GS-7.
GS-9 - You qualify if you possess one year of specialized experience, equivalent to the GS-7 grade level in the Federal, State, or Local government or equivalent public or private sector experience, performing the following duties:
Accessing local and national intelligence information databases to respond to less-complex requests for intelligence information; and
Assisting in the maintenance of computerized intelligence databases; and
Generating statistical/relational reports; and
Collecting operational intelligence reports from various Federal, State and Local government and law enforcement agencies.
OR
Master's or equivalent graduate degree OR 2 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree.
OR
LL.B. Or J.D., if related.
OR
A combination of graduate level education and specialized experience to qualify for this position. Only graduate level education in excess of one year (i.e., 18 semester hours) may be combined with experience under this standard. If using education to qualify, must provide a copy of unofficial or official transcripts.
Education
All academic degrees and course work must be completed at a college or university that has obtained accreditation or pre-accreditation status from an accrediting body recognized by the [Location masked] Department of Education.
Additional information
Selective Service: If you are a male applicant born after December 31, 1959, you must certify that you have registered with the Selective Service System, or are exempt from having to do so under the Selective Service Law.
Federal Regulations state no [Company name masked] employee, his/her spouse, or his/her minor child shall have, directly or indirectly, any financial interest, including compensated employment, stock, or proprietary interest in the alcohol, tobacco, firearms or explosives industries. You should be aware that you may be asked to relinquish any ownership of or interests in the alcohol, tobacco, firearms or explosives industries before a determination can be made whether access to [Company name masked] information, information technology systems, and/or facilities can be authorized.
